chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Al-Hakam ibn Abi Aqeel, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'For me there is an adversary who frequently bears false testimony upon me, and I did not like to compensate him [for his testimony], although I do not know if that is suitable for me or not.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Has it not reached you that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: Do not imprison yourselves and your wealth with false testimonies? For it is not upon a man to restrain himself in his religion, nor is there a sin from his Lord that he should defend that from him, just as if he were to defend by his testimony about an unlawful sexual organ and shedding of unlawful blood, that would be better for him, and similarly is the wealth of the Muslim man.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay witnesses to withdraw false testimony in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the permissibility of paying false witnesses to withdraw their testimony, grounding the ruling in the tradition of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) who cites Imam Ali (AS). It emphasizes that such payment is a pragmatic means of repelling harm (daf' al-darar) rather than a religious penalty, equating the cost to the value of one's honor and wealth. The ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that preventing greater harm (like perjury) justifies the expenditure, even if the witnesses are not strictly 'bribed' in the sense of buying truth.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Al Hakam Bin Abu Aqeel who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For me there is an adversary (enemy) who frequently bears false testimony upon me, and I do not like to fight him, along with that I do not know whether that is correct for me or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘But has it not reached you that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Do not imprison yourselves and your wealth by the false testimonies, for it is not upon a person to restrain himself in his Religion, nor a sin from his Lord<sup>azwj</sup> that he should defend that from him, just as if he were to defend by the testimony about unlawful relationships, and shedding of the unlawful blood, if that was good for him, and similar to that is the wealth of the Muslim person’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Mansur from Yunus from Musa ibn Bakr from al-Hakam ibn abu ‘Aqil who has narrated the following: “I once said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that my opponent brings a great deal of false testimony against me and I dislike to fight back. I do not know if it is the right thing that I do.

He (the Imam) said to me, ’Have you not noticed that ’ Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “Do not leave yourselves and assets hostage to the false testimonies.” If it is not an offense in religion and a sin against his Lord, then there is nothing wrong for a man to defend himself. It is like preventing unlawful sexual relations and unlawful bloodshed by one’s testimony which is good, so also is the case with defending one’s assets.’”
